newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 3.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on April 3. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Suharto has asked Indonesians to be wary of certain groups which he said intended to create chaos in the country. He said the groups would make use of the chaos to hamper the country's development.

The government has decided to postpone a controversial seminar based on a speech by the late president Sukarno until after the May 29 election. Sukarno gave the speech in response to questions in the Provisional Consultative Assembly on his stance on the failed coup attempt blamed on the outlawed Indonesian Communist Party (PKI). The assembly rejected the speech and Sukarno was stripped of his power.

The four factions of the House of Representatives representing the three political parties and the armed forces said President Suharto is still capable of running for office during the 1998-2003 term. The general elections are scheduled for May 29 and the presidential election will be held in 1998.
Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said there was gold at the Busang property in East Kalimantan province but the actual amount had yet to be ascertained.
